text.c6583f5421a83eb3: • URL: '{url}' A path that points to a tileset, service, or file. If the path is relative, it will be relative to the mission's /Missions/{mission} directory. • URL (TMS): Tile Map Service tiles are 256x256 sized images hierarchically organized by zoom level and referenced with x and y coordinates. These are the standard format for web tiles and are the format that MMGIS's auxiliary tiling scripts output. Append /{z}/{x}/{y}.png to your URL. • URL (WMTS): Web Map Tile Service is the same exact concept as TMS but it has an inverted Y-axis. Just like TMS, append /{z}/{x}/{y}.png to your URL. • URL (WMS): Web Map Service tiles are a popular way of publishing maps by professional GIS software. This format is similar to the previous two formats, but more generic and not so well optimized for use in web maps. A WMS image is defined by the coordinates of its corners. A layer (or list of layers) should be provided as an options by appending ?layers=<,another_if_you _want> to your URL. To override WMS parameters append &= again to the URL after the 'layers' parameters. If desired, use &TILESIZE= to change the tile size of the request and layer away from the default of 256. Example URL: http://ows.mundialis.de/services/service?layers=TOPO-WMS,OSM-Overlay-WMS • URL (GeoTiff): '{url_to_tif.tif}' A URL to the .tif. Note that this is not tiled and clients will download the entire file. • COG: '{url_to_cog.tif}' A URL to the .tif and make sure the 'Use TiTiler' option is enabled. • STAC-COLLECTION (Local): 'stac-collection:{collection_name}' - If titiler-pgstac is available, the tileset is the mosaicked COGs within the specified STAC collection from this MMGIS instance. • STAC-COLLECTION (External): 'stac-collection:https://other-mmgis.com/titilerpgstac/collections/{collection_name}' - Reference a STAC collection from an external MMGIS instance. The external server must have CORS enabled and titiler-pgstac available. All COG configuration options (bands, resampling, expressions, etc.) work with external collections.
text.d7968f440b87d84f:
• URL: '{url}' A path to a tileset of RGBA-encoded float32 PNG tiles, typically generated by MMGIS auxiliary scripts (rasterstotiles1bto4b.py). Each pixel stores a 32-bit float as big-endian IEEE 754 RGBA bytes. If the path is relative, it is relative to the Missions/{mission} directory. Append /{z}/{x}/{y}.png to your URL.
• COG: 'COG:{path_or_url_to_cog.tif}' A path or URL to a single-band Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF. MMGIS fetches float32 tiles from TiTiler and decodes them client-side. A relative path is served from the Missions/{mission} directory. TiTiler must be enabled. Example: COG:/Missions/MyMission/Data/elevation.tif
• STAC-COLLECTION (Local): 'stac-collection:{collection_name}' A STAC collection hosted by this MMGIS instance's titiler-pgstac. Tiles are mosaicked COGs from the collection. titiler-pgstac must be enabled. Example: stac-collection:my_elevation_collection
• STAC-COLLECTION (External): 'stac-collection:https://other-mmgis.com/titilerpgstac/collections/{collection_name}' A STAC collection from an external MMGIS instance. The external server must have CORS enabled and titiler-pgstac available.
text.7e9b94057a9c45fc:
• rgba (default, url source only) RGBA-encoded float32 PNG tiles generated by MMGIS auxiliary scripts.
  • terrainrgb Mapbox TerrainRGB-encoded PNG tiles (.png?algorithm=terrainrgb) — elevation = −10000 + (R×65536 + G×256 + B)×0.1. Smaller files with ~0.1 m precision.
  • terrarium Mapzen Terrarium-encoded PNG tiles (.png?algorithm=terrarium) — elevation = R×256 + G + B÷256 − 32768. Smaller files (~10–50 KB/tile) with ~1 cm precision; faster network transfer.
  • npy (COG/STAC) NumPy binary tiles (.npy) from TiTiler — raw float32, no compression, fastest for full float32 precision.
  • tif (url source only) GeoTIFF tiles.

text.d8eda21f7b4c3f4e: Attribution information for the dataset. If configured, the attribution will be displayed horizontally below the scalebar when the layer is visible.
text.e379c1326c876a67: Controls which sublayers from the vector tiles are rendered in the 2D map and how they appear. Only sublayers listed here will be shown — all others are hidden. Example: { "building": { "fill": true, "fillColor": "#cccccc", "fillOpacity": 0.6, "weight": 0.5, "color": "#999999" } }
